The reflection intersection fibers at bases 1,2,3 are [3,6],[0,6],[0,3]. Their hull is full-dimensional, contained in C and has the exact three fibers. Reflection preserves its mixed measure and places its full centroid at (2,3). The same-wave extraction theorem bounds all eligible subbody masses by 12.

The lower endpoints (3,0,0) are convex and the upper endpoints (6,6+t,3) concave, so the enlarged hull has the specified exact fibers and stays in C for 0<t≤1. Widths 3,6+t,3 give base centroid 2, and direct vertical integration gives first moment 18+(6+t)^2/2.

For 0<t≤1, 3<c_t<4 implies strict proper cuts on all three fibers at thresholds c_t+1,c_t,c_t−1. Their cap sum is 15+t−3c_t. Rearranging the exact centroid expression gives deficit t(3+t)/(12+t), positive with first-order coefficient 1/4. Independent rational calculations checked the caps and centroid at 96 positive t values.

Checked 97b12ef4ecc6c56e §§1–3 and its earlier interval source. The present proof uses the independently checked general extraction equivalence, while supplying the polygon optimization directly. The same-wave four-interval example shares that optimization but neither maximizes over eligible convex subbodies nor computes the balanced bulge deficit.
